content.bio:
/**
 * About me
 * I’m a Frontend Lead at a SaaS company. I build SaaS
 * products with React, Next.js and TypeScript.
 *
 * {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} in frontend. I started as an engineer
 * and grew into a team lead. I have shipped products
 * from MVP to production in startups and product teams,
 * and I have led the people who build them.
 *
 * What I care about: frontend architecture, developer
 * experience, performance and clean UI systems. I set
 * standards and workflows so a team can ship on its own.
 * I mentor through code review and design discussions.
 */
content.interests:
/**
 * Interests
 * Tooling that removes setup work. Project templates,
 * internal CLIs and docs that let a new engineer ship
 * in the first week.
 *
 * Teaching. I lectured JavaScript and React, and I still
 * like explaining a hard idea until it becomes simple.
 *
 * Hiring and team process. I have run technical
 * interviews and I like building teams that stay
 * easy to join.
 *
 * Data on screen. Custom charts and visualizations,
 * where the interface has to make numbers readable.
 *
 * Automation. Small bots and integrations that take
 * repetitive work off people.
 */
content.skills:
/**
 * Skills
 *
 * Frontend
 * React, Next.js, TypeScript, Redux Toolkit,
 * TanStack Query, Zustand, Tailwind
 *
 * Architecture
 * Frontend architecture, FSD (Feature-Sliced Design),
 * design systems, SSR, performance optimization
 *
 * Leadership
 * Team leadership, mentoring, hiring, code review
 *
 * Tools
 * AWS, CI/CD, Jest, GraphQL
 */
content.games:
/**
 * Games
 * I play World of Warcraft and whatever is new on
 * my PS5. I also like how games are built: a tight
 * loop of input, state and feedback is good practice
 * for frontend thinking.
 *
 * I am building two of my own:
 * Tiny Coop, a cozy idle desktop game about a hen,
 * made in Godot 4 and heading to Steam.
 * Dareboard, a party game app (truth or dare, never
 * have I ever, spin the bottle) in Expo and React
 * Native, coming to the App Store and Google Play.
 *
 * The snake on the home page is a small one: a pure
 * state engine, testable without a canvas.
 */
content.learning:
/**
 * Learning
 * I am self-taught. I learned frontend from
 * documentation, source code and real projects,
 * and I still learn the same way.
 *
 * Frontend changes fast, and so does the way teams
 * work. I try new ideas in small side projects
 * before they reach a team.
 *
 * This site is one of them: Feature-Sliced Design,
 * strict lint rules and a GSAP motion toolkit.
 *
 * Later I taught others: I lectured JavaScript and
 * React to students at an IT school.
 */

step.details: One tick of the snake engine: a pure function from the previous state to the next, so the game logic is testable without a canvas. It moves the head, grows on food and ends the round on a wall or self hit (the excerpt keeps the move and the eating).

keyToDirection.details: Maps a key press to a snake direction. Arrow keys and WASD both work, and shortcuts with Ctrl, Cmd or Alt held are ignored so the game never steals browser shortcuts.
